definition: In this biological imaging context, amplitude means the magnitude or strength of resting-state neural signal activity measured across brain voxels with fMRI. It is used as one of the voxel-wise measures for detecting altered brain function.

reasons: The packet text does not define “amplitude” as a magnitude/strength measure of resting-state neural signal activity.
The packet does not support that amplitude is measured “across brain voxels with fMRI” or that it is “one of the voxel-wise measures for detecting altered brain function.”

The packet provides a general statement that studies report “voxel-wise alterations in measures of neural amplitude,” but it does not substantiate the specific meaning and usage described in the definition.

The packet does not define amplitude as the magnitude or strength of resting-state neural signal activity; it only says resting-state fMRI studies reported voxel-wise alterations in measures of neural amplitude and synchronization.

The claim that amplitude is measured across brain voxels with fMRI is broader than the source supports; the source mentions voxel-wise analyses in resting-state fMRI but does not provide a definition of the measure itself.

The statement that amplitude is used to detect altered brain function is an unsupported generalization beyond the packet’s wording about identifying convergent amplitude and synchronization dysfunction in postpartum depression.
